articles.title: Channing Tatum Reveals Gambit Movie Plans That Were Closer to Deadpool Than Comics
articles.summary: Channing Tatum's Gambit was very nearly the big-screen superhero that almost wasn't. When the actor finally appeared as the beloved Marvel mutant in 2024's Deadpool & Wolverine, it was not only as a means of bringing the character to life but also to make a giant inside joke for fans familiar with Tatum's long history […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Channing Tatum's Gambit was very nearly the big-screen superhero that almost wasn't . When the actor finally appeared as the beloved Marvel mutant in 2024's Deadpool & Wolverine , it was not only as a means of bringing the character to life but also to make a giant inside joke for fans familiar with Tatum's long history of false starts as Gambit on the big screen. Tatum had flirted with playing with the character long enough that it stretched back all the way to 2006's X-Men: The Last Stand , and persisted for decades, seemingly never to be.

Speaking with Entertainment Weekly about his upcoming reprisal as Gambit for Avengers: Doomsday , Tatum opened up about what the plan was for the Gambit solo movie he was attached to back in the 2010s. According to the star, the idea for the film started out as a romantic comedy in the superhero world, exploring "how do you have a relationship when everybody has superpowers?" That said, Tatum went on to note that plans for the movie shifted as they kept developing it, and as Deadpool became more popular, leading to a "naughty" take on Gambit that didn't happen.

Tatum revealed that the success of Deadpool at the time is what spurred the development of the Gambit movie. As fans may recall, even though Ryan Reynolds' film arrived with half the budget of other X-Men movies, it quickly became the highest-grossing movie in the entire series, even beating the ensemble of X-Men: Days of Future Past , with Deadpool 2 even outgrossing the original by a slim margin.

“We were trying to build a character that was gonna fit in with Deadpool,” Tatum told the outlet. “Deadpool, at that time, was a very specific tone that seemed like it was really hard to work with a lot of other superheroes, in a way, because he would make fun of them. So we were like, ‘Let’s create something that’s a little bit more salacious, a little bit more naughty.’ And Gambit’s a very sexual character anyway, so we definitely were playing around with that.”

Across the years that Tatum developed the movie at 20th Century Fox, it went through a slew of directors, including Rupert Wyatt ( Rise of the Planet of the Apes ), Doug Liman ( Edge of Tomorrow ), and Gore Verbinski ( Pirates of the Caribbean ). At one point, according to reports at the time, Tatum even considered directing it himself, with stories later revealing that Shawn Levy was also in talks at one point, later going on to direct Deadpool & Wolverine .

Given how that movie ended, and the fact that Tatum's presence was at least somewhat a joke, the fan response to his take on the character appears to be what led to him being invited back for Avengers: Doomsday . Though Marvel has already confirmed they're using a deleted scene to explain how he survived The Void, Tatum is quick to note that he still hopes he has a future as Gambit down the line, telling the outlet they wouldn't bring any of the scripts to life they developed at Fox, but adding: "There is a version that does exist that I think is pretty good.”

The one thing potentially standing in Channing Tatum's way of staying on as Gambit for the MCU's future is that Marvel is betting big on the X-Men as their bedrock franchise. Marvel Studios has already confirmed much of the cast for the 2028 X-Men movie, which includes all-new stars and no returning actors from the Fox adaptations. It would be quite surprising if that trend ended with Gambit, especially since the new Rogue actress, Inde Navarrette, is 25 to Tatum's 46. But the odds were stacked against Tatum as Gambit for a decade before, and he beat them once.

articles.summary: Avengers: Doomsday's theatrical debut is rapidly approaching, and for many MCU fans, now is the perfect time to binge watch every film, television show, and press release to try and catch every lore detail or hint as to what's to come. Unsurprisingly, there are a number of Marvel projects that have flown under the radar, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday 's theatrical debut is rapidly approaching , and for many MCU fans, now is the perfect time to binge watch every film, television show, and press release to try and catch every lore detail or hint as to what's to come. Unsurprisingly, there are a number of Marvel projects that have flown under the radar, and for fans looking to check out everything the multimedia giant has to offer that also happen to enjoy anime, Disney+ has the perfect fix.

Marvel Future Avengers initially premiered in 2017 before making its way to the streaming giant in 2020. The anime original series follows Makoto, Adi and Chloe, three teenagers who were raised and genetically tampered with by Hydra, who have brainwashed the teens to believe that the Avengers are the true evil threatening the planet. The series ran for two seasons with a total of 39-episodes, making the series a relatively easy commitment to watch from start to finish.

Marvel Future Avengers was produced by Studio Madhouse, a major entity within the anime industry that has also produced massive shonen franchises like One-Punch Man , Hunter x Hunter , and Frieren: Beyond Journey's End . The anime was directed by Yuzo Sato, who also worked on the 2010 Iron Man anime that was also produced by Madhouse, as well as having previously worked on Kaiji: Ultimate Survivor and Hunter x Hunter: Phantom Rouge . The series is filled with cameos featuring iconic characters from across the multiverse.

The core avengers that serve as mentors to the leading trio include Iron Man, Captain America, The Hulk and Thor, as well as bringing in Wasp and giving her a main role in the series. They aren't the only supers that make an appearance over the anime's two seasons, bringing in names like Iron Fist, Doctor Strange, Black Panter, Bucky Barnes, Spider-Man and many, many more. While Future Avengers does have its three anime-original leads, the cameos made by the Avengers aren't just used to bait in new audiences.

Each of the heroes introduced throughout the series are used to push the narrative and each of the main trio's character arcs forward, whether it be to help flesh out the world Future Avengers takes place in, tactical back-up in sticky situations, or even to just provide a mentorship role to the main characters. The anime follows Makoto, Adi, and Chloe as they discover that their lives with Hydra have been an elaborate lie, eventually being taken in by the Avengers and acting as apprentices, going on missions and aiding the team in thwarting Hydra's plans.

Each of the main trio's powers are unique as well, with Makoto, the center and "lead" of the group being capable of using "aerokinesis," which allows him to manipulate high-powered winds to disrupt battlefields and can create defensive shields of concentrated air as well as being able to fly. Adi is a "technopath" who is able to innately hack into computer systems and control machines with his mind. Tony Stark provides Adi with a special device and suit that amplifies his capabilities. The female lead, Chloe, is a shapeshifter with powers similar to that of Mystique — capable of replicating the physical form and voice of anyone she sees.

As of writing, there has been no announcement that Marvel Future Avengers will receive a third season . The second season of the anime came to an end in 2018 as the Avengers, accompanied by Makoto, Adi, and Chloe face off against Maximus and his forces. Despite the fact that the anime has no continuation beyond the first two seasons, Marvel Future Avengers did receive a tie-in manga that released alongside the anime from 2017 to 2018 that was later compiled into a 6-chapter volume.

The manga follows the same core premise as Season One of the anime, but condenses some of the story down for those who want to binge the series quickly. But for now, this is the only easily accessible Marvel anime to check out right now. Have you ever seen Future Avengers ? Let us know in the comments.

Marvel veteran Sebastian Stan is sticking up for last year's " Thunderbolts ," despite it being one of the lowest-grossing MCU movies.

In the team-up movie, he reprised his role as Bucky Barnes, aka the Winter Soldier, alongside Florence Pugh as Yelena Belova and David Harbour as the Red Guardian to form the Thunderbolts, a new group in the MCU. They later renamed themselves the New Avengers, made up of Wyatt Russell as U.S. Agent, Lewis Pullman as Sentry and Hannah John-Kamen as Ghost, and the team will return in next month's "Avengers: Doomsday." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Ariana Grande’s ‘Eternal Sunshine Tour’ Concert Movie and Making-of Documentary to Stream on Peacock in December Ariana Grande Appears on 'Tonight Show' After Months Away From Public Eye

After releasing in May 2025, "Thunderbolts" ended its box office run with $382 million worldwide, ranking as the fifth lowest total out of all 38 MCU films. The only movies below it are "Black Widow" ($379 million), "Captain America: The First Avenger" ($370 million), "The Incredible Hulk" ($264 million) and "The Marvels" ($206 million). They're all a far cry from this summer's "Spider-Man: Brand New Day," which is the second biggest MCU movie with $2.5 billion (behind the highest-grossing film ever, "Avengers: Endgame" with $2.94 billion).

"I think it's just when you've had a studio and you've had Marvel and it's been so many years where they've just been knocking it out of the park, $350 million global, something like that, it just suddenly doesn't seem that much," Stan said on "Next Big Picture." "But it's insane how much money that is."

He added, "For us, it felt like a success. I know a lot of care went into that and it had more nuance to it in terms of some of the recent ones, from my point of view at least, dealing with real issues like mental health and depression and so on." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.title: Danny Boyle Said Robert Pattinson Would Make A Great Bond Years Ago. Now He’s Backing An Actor To Be His Villain
articles.summary: Let’s throw some names into the mix!
articles.content:
In 2019, Danny Boyle, who was originally named the director for the James Bond film that eventually became No Time to Die , suggested Robert Pattinson as the man to take over as the next person to play Bond. Now, seven years later, that prediction has come true, as Pattinson was officially named the next 007 last week. Boyle isn’t done making suggestions, however, but now he’s switched to who should play the villain: Jack O’Connell.

O’Connell was one of the (many) actors who were rumored to be in the running for Bond 26 before Amazon MGM and director Denis Villeneuve ultimately decided to go with Pattinson, and I think his take on O’Connell as the villain is also an inspired idea as well. Along with who could be the next “Bond Girl,” the next Bond Villain is another big casting chip that still needs to fall soon before filming kicks off, hopefully in 2027.

O’Connell isn’t the only name being bandied about to play James Bond ’s next villain. Another actor who has worked with Boyle before, Cillian Murphy , has been a popular choice among fans. Barry Keoghan, who worked with Murphy on the 2026 movie schedule in Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man (which was headed up by Bond 26 writer Steven Knight), is also a top pick. Idris Elba, whom many hoped (including me) could be the next Bond, though even he admitted he’s too old for the role now, is also a common name thrown out there (and honestly, maybe my pick).

articles.title: Denis Villeneuve Pledges Traditional, "Unapologetic" Bond: "Not Here to Change the DNA"
articles.summary: The director teases a classic approach to his Amazon MGM film starring Robert Pattinson: "I love the way the character behaves."
articles.content:
Denis Villeneuve says his highly anticipated reboot of the James Bond franchise isn't going to back away from the "unapologetic" traits of the iconic character.

The Dune: Part Three director teased his vision of 007 in a new interview and suggested that he's a traditionalist when it comes to portraying Ian Fleming's suave, seductive, killer spy.

"I love traditions," Villeneuve told Time . "I love the unapologetic way the character behaves, the panache. I’m not here to change the DNA of James Bond. I’m here to embrace it, to bring it to the world of today. I’m a hardcore James Bond fan, and I want other fans to have fun watching my film. Of course, it will be tainted by my sensibility. But I wake up every morning with a stupid smile because it’s a world of pure cinematic pleasure." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies 'Twilight' Director Reveals Robert Pattinson Inspired James Bond Line in 2008 Film: "We Were Seeing the Future" Movies 'Avengers: Doomsday' Eyes $270M Opening as 'Dune: Part Three' Also Heads for Big Start

The comments are interesting because of the cultural debate that's surrounded Bond in recent years, and how the later Daniel Craig films attempted to wrestle with the question of how the often sexist cinematic character dating back to the 1960s should operate in the modern age.

How much Villeneuve was thinking of Pattinson during his comments is unclear — the interview was conducted one week before The Batman actor was publicly announced as the new Bond .

Meanwhile, speculation has shifted to who will play the film's villain, with oddsmakers thinking Tom Hardy has a strong shot (indeed, given Pattinson's slight frame, choosing a physically imposing villain would make for a nicely formidable antagonist). So what does his morning actually look like? According to longtime trainer Bobby Rich, one thing never changes. The Daily Ultimate Essentials Pro is a drink mix that's part of the lineup at IM8, the supplements brand Beckham co-founded with health sciences company Prenetics after years of juggling bottle after bottle.

"I've often felt overwhelmed by how many different products it takes to truly support your body," he wrote in a letter to IM8 customers. The fix was Daily Ultimate Essentials Pro, a single morning drink that replaces 16 supplements.

Denis Villeneuve says he is "deeply disappointed" that Disney chose to release box office juggernaut Avengers: Doomsday over the same December 18 weekend as the third instalment in his Dune franchise.

Dune is not a mammoth like the Avengers, but it’s a sexy little animal that has a lot of firepower, and I hope we will survive. articles.title: Harry Potter Confirms 1 Book Character Is a Puppet in HBO's Reboot, But That Will Change
articles.summary: HBO HBO's Harry Potter TV series has been clear from the jump that the only reason to reboot the property after eight movies and more than $7.7 billion at the box office is an increased fidelity to the source material. True to their word, plenty of details have been released about the series, including new footage, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google HBO's Harry Potter TV series has been clear from the jump that the only reason to reboot the property after eight movies and more than $7.7 billion at the box office is an increased fidelity to the source material . True to their word, plenty of details have been released about the series, including new footage, that show they're bringing in characters, set details, and even story points that were excised from the movie adaptations . Now we have an example of the series playing the long game with one character.

In a new post on the official Harry Potter website, details about HBO's show and how it will bring the magical creatures to life arrived this week, confirming that Ron's pet Scabbers will appear, and he'll be a puppet. According to the site, Scabbers is being brought to life in the series as a "startlingly realistic" animatronic that is a "cross-between a soft toy and a robot." A few different versions of Scabbers were created for different scenes across the TV series, pointing out a "sleeping Scabbers" for the Hogwarts Express, but the biggest details is one Potter fans know well, that Ron's rat is missing a toe, just another example of how the show is planning for the future.

The final detail that the Harry Potter website teased about Scabbers in the HBO reboot is "for those of you wondering… He has got that missing toe." Fans of the series know exactly what that means, because Scabbers isn't just an ordinary rat. It's not revealed until the events of Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban , a story that will seemingly be the third season of the planned TV show, that Scabbers is actually revealed to be a human in disguise.

The entire time that Scabbers has been Ron's pet rat, he's actually Peter Pettigrew in his Animagus form, having previously cut off one of his fingers. Prior to the events of the books, Peter is revealed to have been a member of the Marauders, but later joined forces with Voldemort and faked his death as part of an elaborate scheme to frame Sirius Black for betraying Harry Potter's parents, as well as killing several Muggles.

As fans may recall, the seeds for Scabbers being a little different are set up in the first two books, even if it's certainly a surprise when the big reveal happens. To that end, this marks yet another indicator that the HBO Harry Potter series is gearing up for long-term plans, even if we have no idea who will be playing the role of Peter Pettigrew when that batch of episodes finally arrives.

Production on Harry Potter Season 2 is already happening, even with a few weeks left before the series actually makes its premiere on HBO, but that's far from the most distinct indicator that the show is playing the long game. Set photos of Dumbledore star John Lithgow made their way online during the first wave of production, which sparked a rumor that the series may be filming scenes with his character that were actually for much later in the show's plans, since the actor himself is already 79 years old.

One actual confirmation that we have about the show's long-term plans as a series is the show's Forbidden Forest set, which star Nick Frost revealed had been constructed so that it would last for the next ten years, adding: “They’re calling it a living set because it grows as we shoot."

HBO's Harry Potter is scheduled to premiere on Christmas Day.

articles.title: Supremely Scarce Umbreon Pokémon Card Sells for $216,000 at Auction, Nearly 22 Times Its 2025 Price
articles.summary: Image Courtesy The Pokémon Company An eminently rare Umbreon Pokémon TCG card just reached more than $200,000 at auction, adding another enormous six-figure result to an already extraordinary year for Pokémon card collectors. The 2013 Black & White Black Star Promo Umbreon #BW93, graded PSA 10 Gem Mint, commanded $216,000 with buyer's premium during Fanatics Collect's 253rd Weekly auction on […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google An eminently rare Umbreon Pokémon TCG card just reached more than $200,000 at auction, adding another enormous six-figure result to an already extraordinary year for Pokémon card collectors. The 2013 Black & White Black Star Promo Umbreon #BW93, graded PSA 10 Gem Mint, commanded $216,000 with buyer's premium during Fanatics Collect's 253rd Weekly auction on November 22.

Although the Moonlight Pokémon has become accustomed to attracting astronomical prices, this particular result has an interesting wrinkle. Another PSA 10 example sold for $264,000 in September, meaning the latest sale actually fell $48,000 short of the existing record. Nevertheless, that's an extraordinary amount for a card originally distributed in a collection box, particularly considering a Gem Mint example fetched less than $10,000 just last year. With only 14 PSA 10 copies currently recorded, this Umbreon has developed into one of the more formidable (and unheralded) Eeveelution grails of the Black & White era. Let's take a gander at how it got there.

All-Time Record Sale: $264,000 in September 2026

Umbreon #BW93 may lack the widespread recognition of Evolving Skies’ famed Moonbreon Special Illustration Rare or the tremendous cachet of the iconic POP Series 5 Umbreon Gold Star, but the latest auction result demonstrates that collectors are willing to spend an outrageous amount of money for a pristine copy.

According to PSA's sales records , another Gem Mint copy commanded $264,000 through Fanatics Collect on September 28. The November result represents an 18.2% decline from that previous benchmark, which is hardly insignificant when dealing with such an expensive piece of cardboard. Still, $216,000 would have been an almost unimaginable sum for this particular promo just a few years ago. The card's 14-copy PSA 10 population certainly helps explain its appeal, especially as other Black & White-era Pokémon cards have recently commanded similarly staggering prices .

Beyond that, PSA's documented sales history includes a Gem Mint example that sold for just $9,900 on eBay in July 2025. Compared with that transaction, the latest $216,000 auction result represents an increase of $206,100, or approximately 2,082%, in less than a year and a half—nearly 22 times the previous price.

Intriguingly, the September record-setting copy was the very same card that sold for $9,900 in 2025, according to its PSA certification number. The market has clearly undergone a dramatic transformation in a remarkably short period, even if the latest result suggests that prices aren't necessarily destined to climb indefinitely. Given that six exceedingly rare Eeveelution cards combined for nearly $600,000 in an earlier auction this year, Umbreon's latest showing fits rather neatly into a broader pattern of extraordinary demand for Eevee's various evolutions.

Unlike the traditional booster-pack chase cards that dominate many high-end Pokémon auctions, Umbreon #BW93 originated in the Sylveon Collection, which was released on November 15, 2013. This collection box celebrated Sylveon's arrival in the TCG and included four Black & White booster packs, a Sylveon figurine, a Fairy Energy card, and nine promotional Pokémon cards featuring Eevee and all eight of its evolutions.

Umbreon was numbered BW93 and featured a distinctive Cosmos holofoil treatment and artwork credited to the entire The Pokémon Company Art Team (something only 15 other cards can boast). While this illustration had already appeared in Japan during the Pokémon Center's 2012 Eevee Collection campaign, its 2013 English release offered collectors a particularly attractive version of the fan-favorite Dark-type Pokémon, complete with its glowing yellow rings, elegantly mysterious aura, and moody coloration.

We've already witnessed three Southern Islands promos combine for $972,000 at auction , while Umbreon Gold Star's staggering $738,100 sale offers further evidence that collectors have an almost insatiable appetite for Eevee’s Dark-type evolution. Whether this particular Black & White promo eventually surpasses its $264,000 record remains to be seen, but one thing is crystal-clear: Umbreon is perfectly capable of turning a once-modest retail collectible into something worth more than a luxury sedan.

Dave Keuning , guitarist for The Killers , said that he survived a "major stroke" two weeks ago that had a "40% chance of survival" but he's still able to "play guitar just as good as before." He revealed the news on Thanksgiving, along with announcing the birth of his daughter.

"Happy Thanksgiving, everyone! Three months ago, we had our baby girl, Odette," Keuning wrote. "Two weeks ago, I had a major stroke, and thanks to my wife acting fast, I went straight to the hospital and into surgery. The first hour after a stroke is critical when it comes to getting to the hospital. I had a blood clot in my brain that cut off the blood supply to the entire right side of my brain. By the time I arrived at the hospital, I was blind in one eye and had lost function on my left side, but I still wasn’t able to realize I was having a stroke. The doctors said I had a 40% chance of survival and I would have disabilities after, but by some miracle I am fine." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Ariana Grande Appears on 'Tonight Show' After Months Away From Public Eye Ariana Grande Says 'Petal' Music Video Backlash Felt Like 'Black Mirror' and 'I Wouldn’t Change a Thing. Keuning thanked his Killers bandmates, including lead singer Brandon Flowers, drummer Ronnie Vannucci Jr. and bassist Mark Stoermer, for their support during his recovery.

articles.title: Record Store Day Black Friday's Most Wanted, 2026: Beatles, Noah Kahan, Bruce Springsteen, Prince, Sombr, Billy Joel, Katseye and Other Vinyl Must-Finds
articles.summary: Record Store Day is back in black. As you likely already know, RSD is a semiannual holiday for vinyl hounds, with the Black Friday edition being a less jam-packed adjunct to the primary event in April — meaning that, this year, for instance, there are "only" 188 titles being released, almost exactly half of the […]
articles.content:
14,500 copies on 4x LP; 3,700 copies on 2x CD; black vinyl

Springsteen buffs will not always agree on favorite individual shows from his and the band's 50-year-plus history, but it's hard to imagine a single fan not considering the "Born to Run" era to be peak form. or not taking a serious interest in this rendering of a long and loose New Year's Eve concert at the close of 1975. The only question might be which physical format you want it in, since Sony is offering it for Record Store Day Black Friday in both LP and CD form. The much greater amount of vinyl pressed indicates an obvious consumer preference for vinyl nowadays, but with a concert this length, some may reconsider whether they want to flip sides seven times to get it all and opt for compact disc. Whether you pick up a vinyl slipcase or CD jewel box, there are succinct but sweet liner notes from Erik Flannigan, who points out that, yes, that is the band (except for Bruce) decked out in tuxedos in the photographs in the packaging. Good thing any formality about this wonderful show ends there.

10,000 copies of vinyl 12-inch EP; Alpenglow-colored vinyl

Kahan's exclusive releases have been among the biggest draws at many recent Record Store Days, which is no surprise, given the ongoing presence of two of his studio albums in the top 10 and stadium tours that sell out instantaneously. Fans will already be familiar with the four songs on this EP — "Lighthouse," "Staying Still," A Few of Your Own" and "Orbiter" — since they first appeared as bonus tracks on a digital deluxe edition of his smash "The Great Divide" album (and "Orbiter" is a proper single). But having the four tracks partitioned off into their own separate physical release will be irresistible to diehard stickheads.

It's not like you're going to get any songs here that you didn't already get on the recent "Rubber Soul" 60th anniversary super-deluxe edition… or, for that matter, that you haven't had access to since 1966. But then, that's the point: This single LP is a recreation of the exact album that U.S. Beatles fans got in '66, down to the original stereo mix. But that's been out of print for a long time… and has never been uin print as a gold-colored record, which is the main novelty here. The good news for Beatles collectors is that it's been pressed in numbers that fall at the very top end of pressings for Record Store Day; the bad news is that 15,000 still won't last long.

9,400 copies on 3x vinyl; 2,700 copies on 2x CD; vinyl color is crystal blue curaçao

The Prince estate is really making the most out of the fact that it had a pro-shot film of Prince's six-month 2006-7 residency in Las Vegas in the can. A film of "3121 Las Vegas Live" will briefly hit the big screen in early December, followed by a Blu-Ray edition for home consumption. In the meantime, if you want a physical manifestation of just the music, Record Store Day participant shops are the place to go. The performance captured here starts at a slow simmer but quickly heats up. Suffice it to say that, after hearing this purely audio version, I'll be lined up for the movie.

Every time there is a new CD boxed set in the ongoing series of Joni Mitchell archival anthologies, a single live performance from that collection gets broken out to have its own separate LP edition for Record Store Day. No complaints at all about that. This '72 concert is all Joni, accompanying herself on guitar, piano or dulcimer, all the way to a closing "Circle Game" that does have her suddenly surrounded by a chorus of famous and unfamous friends. Some will prefer Mitchell in her purest early-ish form here, and some may prefer the big band era that followed. But hearing the purity of that voice with an emphasis on the then-recent "Blue" and then-forthcoming "For the Roses" is a knockout experience. The only thing more you could wish for is a gatefold jacket instead of putting both discs in a single sleeve (the product description promises gatefold, but it's not), or liner notes, but it's still a handsome-looking as well as -sounding package.

The last Billy Joel live album, released for Record Store Day Black Friday 2025, was "Live From Long Island," pressed in a quantity of 1,500 copies — and fans are still pissed about that. (Resale copy prices are not completely exorbitant, but they do go for more than $100.) Fortunately, the record company got the message and is putting three times that many of this followup on sale, 4,600, although that still may not completely sate the market for live Joel. It's a spirited set, from a hyperactive "Angry Young Man" opening forward, recorded Dec. 5, 1976 at Connecticut College for a TV special. It includes 15 never-before-released tracks from either the original live shows or a followup that was done to get better takes for the special. The blurb on the back cover promises that four more tracks will be included in a "Turnstiles" 50th anniversary boxed set coming out next year. But few Joel fans will complain about that wait given the wealth of heretofore unreleased music here.

Sombr: 7,500 copies on silver vinyl

Boone: 5,000 copies on black and white galaxy vinyl

The Sombr and Benson Boone releases are very similar, in that each is a first-time vinyl issue of the EP that started their major-label careers before they broke a lot bigger with a full album that followed. Bot EPs are also mellower than some of the hit music that followed for these artists — Sombr lives up to his name more here. His EP, at four tracks, is less expansive than Boones, which runs to eight songs, and comes with a 12-by-24 insert that has a poster image on one side and lyrics on the other. Apart from their musical merits, both discs just look fab, pulled out of their sleeves and placed into the wild.

Withers: 2,600 copies on LP; 1,300 copies on CD; LP is black vinyl

Various artists/Sweet Relief: 1,200 copies

Now here's an unofficial two-fer anyone should think about picking up and turning into a double feature, even if their simultaneous release, coming from different labels, may be coincidental. First, there's Withers' own 1974 performance, captured for British TV. You can tell the audio is unedited: Withers is heard telling the studio audience that some of his band members are out sick, and in one case restarting a speech. The relaxed feel carries over to the superlative songs. Meanwhile, I have to give an even more enthusiastic endorsement to a double-LP tribute album put together as a benefit for the Sweet Relief Foundation that includes all-new tracks. I was hoping the great Chris Pierce — one of the closest things we have to a modern-day Withers right now — would be one of the artists chosen, and to my sweet relief, he was, contributing "Better Off Dead." There are also choice cuts from Rickie Lee Jones, Lady Blackbird, Marilyn McCoo and Billy Davis Jr., Ben Harper and others who know how to mix their own spin on things with takes that feel faithful to Withers' vibe.

2,600.copies of six-LP boxed set; multiple vinyl colors

Rhino has gotten in the habit of issuing one complete boxed set per RSD event for a renowned artist from the Warner-Elektra catalog of riches, from John Prine to Devo. This one for 10,000 Maniacs, composed of all the albums the group put out before Natalie Merchant split to go solo in 1993, is being seen by fans as a very necessary corrective to the fact that a lot of that stuff has been out of print on vinyl forever. Four studio albums are joined by the pre-fame compendium "Hope Chest" and a newly assembled rarities disc full of delectable covers. Merchant is credited with helping oversee the package, including the design of the physical elements, although the liner notes (which are very good) do not include interviews with her or any of the bandmates who continue to carry on without her. It's worth noting that all of the albums included except the rarities LP are due to be issued individually early next year, if it's just one or two you need to pick up. But as a fan from their earliest major-label days, I couldn't imagine not getting the whole thing right now. A matter of curiosity: All of the box and LP packaging here changes the band's name to Ten Thousand Maniacs from 10,000 Maniacs (although the numerical usage pops up in the liner notes). Some elements of the album cover art have been changed, along with the band-name logos — it has to be a Merchant thing. But if you pick up the individual issues in a few months, apparently the name and artwork will be as we remember them. (The fact that the albums in this box have different covers is further cemented by the lack of barcodes.) Those peculiarities aside, t's a great trip down maniacal memory lane.

Jepsen has been nothing but prolific in this era, first issuing "Day and Night" as a hefty double-album, then adding eight additional tracks onto the original 24 for a deluxe edition, "Day and Night (Continued)." that runs to an hour and 55 minutes of material. Some things may be more easily digested in smaller chunks, of course, and this EP — also titled "Day and Night (Continued)" — breaks out those eight fresher tracks and gives them their first appearance in a physical format. Plus, you get still more from her photo shoot at Eagle Rock's Casa Bianca, the best pizza joint in L.A., and if that's not reason enough to pick it up, you've got eight more.

The previous RSD exclusive editions of the "Wicked" and "Wicked: For Good" sold out so quickly, I never did actually catch a glimpse of either of them in my many store visits. That will probably prove true for this combined set that packages both soundtracks together in a 4-LP set in a slipcase with a poster. (The track list, if accurate as rendered online, leaves out the bonus track that was added onto the original RSD "Wicked" issue.) Good luck hunting this down, unless it turns out every franchise fan was sated by the previous two releases after all, which isn't likely. It's gonna be popular.

3,300 2x LP copies; black vinyl

The first of several releases we'll mention here produced by "jazz detective" Zefv Feldman is a welcome incursion into the wonderful world of Blakey. It comtbines two previously unreleased performances in Paris, the first from 1963 and sporting famous players like Freddie Hubbard and Wayne Shorter, the second with a different ensemble in '68. "Moons" were on the band leader's mind, as the collection includes the two big musical moon shots of the era, "Blue Moon" and "Moon River." The latter opens the collection and might give Henry Mancini a heart attack if he were still around to have one — it's like "Moon River" on amphetamines (not speaking literally, friends, just figuratively), and it's quite a fantastic flood. The liner notes booklet is copious as with almost any Feldman-related release, and even though a CD edition will follow for the general market in a week, it's always worth picking up the limited-edition vinyl versions of these releases just for the larger type and photographs. And, sure, the wide-open grooves, too.

5,000 copies of 2x LP; on “Third Pyramid Pink” vinyl

I would have taken an interest in a B-52s live set anyway, but this one turns out to be particularly a wowser because of the addition of a three-man horn section that really helps some of the songs rock in an augmented way. Fans may already know this Roseland Ballroom NYC '82 performance from when it was included in the "Ancient Culture: Mesopotamia Revisited" set, but for those of us who didn't have that, or anyone who did but just likes a good breakout, it's a delightful revelation of the band at its early '80s peak.

3,500 copies of 12-inch vinyl EP; red vinyl

Cher had not released any original material in many years until she came back with a Christmas project that included some songs newly written to add to the holiday tuneage canon. With this EP spinoff, the emphasis is on the dance-ier chestnuts, including three different mixes of "DJ Play a Christmas Song" and an added duet with Kelly Clarkson. The lady-in-red cover shot is different from any previous artwork in her Christmas-music campaign, too.

2,600 copies of 2x LP; black vinyl

Another archival production from Zev Feldman, who is stretching out from being seen as "just" a jazz guy with his Bobby Womack and Marianna Faithful releases this Record Store Day. Womack can also stretch out, as it turns out, with two numbers in this live set that go past the 12-minute mark, "You're Welcome, Stop on By" and "Communication" are both over 12 minutes long. Recorded in Paris in 1976, where the liner notes say he was having a higher profile at the time than in the U.S., this collection feels essential as a revelation of just what an expansive showman he was as well as crafter of classic soul singles.

Sax man Getz is the only one with his name above the title on this release, but for the first three of its six sides, legendary guitarist João Gilberto is his equal costar. Together, they recreate the magic they'd made together in a historic studio teaming in one of the few live shows they did together to follow that. All the music here was previously released by Resonance more than a decade ago, but this three-LP set for the first time combines two albums — one of Getz with Gilberto in SF, one without — into an exemplary single package (and the Getz-only half of the equation never made it onto vinyl before). The multiple interviews or essays in the copious liner notes even include a sizable explanation of the bossa nova craze that finds a kind of quiet culmination here.

5,000 copies of single-sided EP

We were not able to preview this particular release, so we cannot vouch for what the "dance break" versions of three of Katseye's most popular songs sound like — "Debut," "Gnarly" and "Gabriela." But we can tell you the way it will fly off the shelves will be gnarly indeed. All three mixes are congregated on one side of the vinyl, with a mystery etching on the other. Each copy is said to includes two out of six "randomly selected unique photocards," so fans will be figuring out how to get around the one-copy-per-customer rule in most stores, as if this needed an incentive to sell out faster.

This is the "Bitches Brew"-era Miles who took free jazz into the land of psychedelia, if you hadn't already guessed that from the cover art by his favorite cover painter in the '60s, Mati Klarwein. It might as well have been recorded at the Fillmore, even though Davis actually had his all-star quintet (Wayne Shorter, Chick Corea, Dave Holland and Jack DeJohnette) in Copenhagen for a TV taping. The music has previously been heard on a DVD and on a one-time vinyl pressing of just a few hundred copies, but this mastering is said to be a revelation even for the relatively small number of cultists who've already heard this dynamic performance in some form.

10,000 copies; "Derpy Sussie Splatter" vinyl

The hunt for "Kpop Demon Hunters" collectibles never stops. Record Store Day just had dual editions of the soundtrack that were quick and easy sellouts, but that could hardly stand in the way of yet another version — and surely not the last — this one featuring fresh art created by official "Demon Hunters" production designer Mingjue Helen Chen and visual development artist Marion Bordeyne. We'll let the product description do the rest of the talking: "This Derpy Sussie Splatter vinyl includes exclusive holographic art on both the front cover and triple gatefold, 3 of 6 mini inserts, 1 of 3 holographic mini inserts, a sticker sheet, and an oversized poster." You might have to take their word for it since it won't be surprising if most or all of the copies are gone by the time you get your lazy post-Thanksgiving butt to the shop.

1,800 copies on three-sided 2x LP set; black vinyl

We're still morning Faithful's passing, so it's moving to hear her in her prime, or one of her primes, in a performance captured in 1983, after a comeback run of three acclaimed albums on Island, including of course "Broken English." The tape of the D.C. set ends with the title track from that latter album and is missing a few final songs from the actual performance, so it's spread across three sides and the fourth is devoted to an etching of a William Blake quote in concentric-circle script.

Fountains of Wayne's final album before their breakup sometimes gets undervalued because it's their least comical, most sober outing, perhaps reflecting the more dominant influence of Chris Collingwood, versus the wryer touch favored by Adam Schlesinger, who'd run the show more on the preceding record. Regardless, there's wit enough here, along with some of the band's starker songs. It's been challenging for FoW fans to complete their vinyl collections, since this fast went out of print after a single pressing in 2001. Even now, 2,000 is not a lot, but it'll be at least enough to satisfy some of us who never stopped believing that this brilliant group had it going on.

As the title and cover hint, this is a collection of cover songs these Dolls have done over the years, and what great taste they've had in other bands, as evidenced in a collection that runs from the Plimsouls' "A Million Miles Away" to the Kinks' "Catch Me Now, I'm Falling," with stops for Tom Petty, INXS, Prince and… Supertramp! (A CD and digital release will follow a week after this vinyl exclusive.)

We did not get a review copy of this, but we're going to guess from the product description alone that it might be fun, with or without actually listening to what's in the grooves, just from looking at them. "Zoetrope" discs have been a thing for a while, turning vinyl into animation, but this is the first one we can recall seeing that is billed as a 3D zoetrope disc, with cardboard glasses to put on to enjoy the effect. We look forward to hearing whether the effect of watching that is as mind-bending as the Gizzard boys' music typically is, and what substances it is best combined with.

2,215 copies of six-45-rpm-singles boxed set; different marbled color variations

Jazz Dispensary dispenses something worth picking up for every single RSD edition, and this time they've eschewed the usual single-LP compilation format to put out a box of singles. It comes in a candy-style box, with six different vintage singles in different but equally delicious-looking colors, plus some glow-in-the-dark 45 adapters as a bonus. As usual, even though the description calls these "jazz," the music therein leans more toward the funk side of the fence, from Eddie Jefferson's honestly groovy "Psychedelic Sally" to Patrice Rushen's kinda-weird "Kickin' Back." Obscure but charming singles from Rusty Bryant, Idris Muhammad, Pleasure and Johnny Hammond are also represented. Will you play these a lot, or easily find shelf space for an odd-shaped package? Probably no in both cases, yet it's kind of irresistible as a hep novelty package nonetheless.

What could be better for celebrating the season than NRBQ's 1978 "Merry Christmas From NRBQ" EP? Very possibly, a modern expansion of that project that extends it to 19 tracks, 10 of them making their vinyl debut, one (the closing "Auld Lang Syne") getting its premiere altogether. We weren't able to preview this package to tell you whether they do or don't rock out the newly added "Jesus Loves Me" and "The Christmas Song," but we hope to score a copy and fill in that part of the NRB-FAQ.

articles.title: Florence Pugh Had Big Balls When She Called Little Women's Director And Asked Her To Hold Her Spot
articles.summary: Thank goodness she did this!
articles.content:
Florence Pugh is one of the biggest movie stars we have right now. I mean she’s in both films bearing the Dunesday nickname on the 2026 movie schedule for crying out loud! So, I’d expect a director to move mountains in order to get her on their film. It turns out Pugh had balls of steel even before she earned her A-list status. When she was just 22, she was faced with the ultimate Sophie’s Choice of movie roles.

This, ladies and gentleman is yet another reason why Florence Pugh is the major name she is. She clearly understood at the time that she had stumbled onto two incredible parts, and she didn't want to choose, despite others telling her she must. With that in mind, she pushed aside any fears and decided to simply ask for what she wanted. Here’s what happened next, per her interview with Elle :

Pugh ended up shooting Midsommar first with writer/director Ari Aster, which proved to be a taxing shoot for the actress . It was all worth it because the A24 film has since become known as one of the best horror movies of all time , with Dani’s May Queen and the Bear also becoming a popular Halloween costume, too. Pugh later also got a Midsommar tattoo to immortalize the movie on her body.

Right after she made Midsommar in Hungary, Pugh ventured to Massachusetts to make Little Women with writer/director Greta Gerwig alongside a cast including Timothée Chalamet, Saoirse Ronan, Emma Watson , Laura Dern and Meryl Streep . Whew, what a list! Little Women went on to give Pugh her first (and still only) Oscar nomination for Best Supporting Actress. Oh, and it also changed how we think about Amy March being a villain in the literary classic, probably forever.

articles.title: Dune 3 Director Breaks Silence on Avengers: Doomsday Releasing the Same Day, "I Was Deeply Disappointed"
articles.summary: Marvel Studios Avengers: Doomsday has been dominating the headlines all week, and largely overshadowing the fact that it is but one of two of the biggest movies of the year releasing on the same day. The other film is Dune: Part Three, director Denis Villeneuve's highly anticipated finale to the Dune movie trilogy. Fans quickly gave Friday, […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avengers: Doomsday has been dominating the headlines all week, and largely overshadowing the fact that it is but one of two of the biggest movies of the year releasing on the same day. The other film is Dune: Part Three , director Denis Villeneuve's highly anticipated finale to the Dune movie trilogy. Fans quickly gave Friday, December 18th the unofficial nickname of "Dunesday," and there are many who are hoping it will be the next double-feature cultural phenomenon like "Barbenheimer" (the same-day release of Barbie and Oppenheimer ) in 2023 . However, that's not the way that Villeneuve feels about it.

In a new interview with TIME , Denis Villeneuve expresses his own "disappointment" with Marvel Studios' decision to stand on the release date for Avengers: Doomsday . Read below to find out why.

When asked how he feels about the shared release date between Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday , Villeneuve basically explains that intentionally or not, Marvel has triggered some level of his trauma from making and releasing these Dune movies.

"Listen, I will be honest. The first Dune came out at the end of the pandemic. We made a great box office in a very rough environment. But we had the winds against us. Then the second movie, same thing. We were meant to release in the fall, and we had to release at the end of winter because of the two Hollywood strikes. We had success, but it was not easy," Villeneuve said. "The third time, I said to myself, 'Finally, there is no pandemic, no strike in sight. We will have a normal release.' Then Disney put the biggest franchise of all time against us. I’m no fool. Those movies are a mammoth. So I was deeply disappointed."

Many would probably agree that Villeneuve has a valid point: The first two Dune films definitely had their respective releases thrown off by the two biggest hits to the entertainment industry this decade: the 2020 Pandemic, and the 2023 Hollywood Strikes. And, to the credit of Villeneuve and Dune, both films did well at the box office (a combined $1.14 billion against a total budget of $355 million), and launched a (moderately) successful HBO spinoff series, Dune: Prophec y (Season 2 premiering in 2027), and won a combined 8 Oscars for its technical and stylistic achievements. A third film was well-earned – as was the chance for the franchise to enjoy at least one normal release date window.

Instead, like the pot of Dune: Part Three , there will be a massive battle for the throne (box office), with both Marvel and Warner Bros. careening toward incursion. Dune Part: Three has already achieved a key strategic victory over Avengers: Doomsday : securing the IMAX premium format.

"We had committed to this date, to IMAX. It was impossible to move. So I accepted my fate, praying to the gods of cinema," Villeneuve continued. " Dune is not a mammoth like the Avengers, but it’s a sexy little animal that has a lot of firepower, and I hope we will survive. It could be one of the biggest box-office weekends of all time because of both movies. Am I in competition with the Avengers? Absolutely not. It’s a T. rex. But I stand proud because I think the film delivers."

Speaking personally, I think both Denis Villeneuve and Avengers: Doomsday director Joe and Anthony Russo will all end up toasting champagne (perhaps even together?) at the end of opening weekend. I will one-hundred-percent be seeing both films, possibly more than once in subsequent weeks of release. Both films are major cinematic events that represent the end of major chapters in cinema, and there is so much overlap in the primary fanbases of both films that it their releases will become a "Barbenheimer" cultural event, guaranteed.

We'll all be watching how the box office battle plays out when Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday are released on December 18th.

The first title from Yuasa's new studio ame pippin unveiled images to The Hollywood Reporter of the main characters from the animated adaptation of Banana Yoshimoto’s novel, Daisy’s Life. The second image shows both animated characters seated together at the roots of a tree, bonding over yakisoba, a Japanese stir-fried noodle dish. Their friendship helps frame the story of Daisy, who, as a child, lost her mother, her only family, in an accident and now grieves that death. Studio ame pippin on Thursday unveiled a short clip from Daisy's Life on X.

“On a long, lonely night during the rainy season, she (Daisy) plays the recorder by herself. As if drawn by the sound, Dahlia appears and becomes the friend who supports Daisy through her isolation. Years later, while Daisy is living and working at her aunt and uncle's yakisoba restaurant, a letter arrives from Brazil. It speaks of the mysterious connection between two lonely souls separated by distance and time,” a synopsis from the producers of Daisy’s Life states.

The film is the first animated feature from ame pippin, the animation studio founded by Yuasa in 2025. Director Yuasa is known for classic films like The Tatami Galaxy and Ping Pong the Animation, and in 2013 co-founded Science SARU with Eunyoung Choi. He directed an episode of Adventure Time and The Night Is Short, Walk on Girl.

Yuasa left Science SARU in 2020 after Keep Your Hands Off Eizouken! and directed Inu-Oh, which earned both Golden Globe and Annie nominations. Character designer Izumi Murakami created the animated characters for Yuasa’s Daisy’s Life adaptation, while production designer Tomotaka Kubo created the film’s settings that envelop Daisy and Dahlia’s time together.

Visual development artist Batiste Perron, color designer Ayaka Nakamura, director of photography Yoshihiro Sekiya and editor Kiyoshi Hirose are also part of Yuasa’s creative team.

articles.title: Denis Villeneuve "Deeply Disappointed" Disney Put 'Avengers: Doomsday' Against 'Dune 3'
articles.summary: The director breaks silence on going head-to-head against Marvel's titan on "Dunesday."
articles.content:
Everybody has found it pretty cute, if slightly baffling, that expected box-office heavyweights Dune: Part Three and Avengers: Doomsday are opening on the same day (Dec. 18).

But Dune franchise director Denis Villeneuve isn't amused by going head-to-head with the Marvel titan.

Villeneuve explains in a new interview that he was "deeply disappointed" by the "Dunesday" scheduling, but that Warner Bros. was basically trapped in the slot because the studio had successfully secured an exclusive run on IMAX screens for Dune 3 through the December holidays. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies 'Avengers: Doomsday' Eyes $270M Opening as 'Dune: Part Three' Also Heads for Big Start Movies 'Avengers: Doomsday' Final Trailer Shows Major X-Men Moment

"Listen, I will be honest," he told Time . "The first Dune came out at the end of the pandemic. We made a great box office in a very rough environment. But we had the winds against us. Then the second movie, same thing. We were meant to release in the fall, and we had to release at the end of winter because of the two Hollywood strikes. We had success, but it was not easy. The third time, I said to myself, 'Finally, there is no pandemic, no strike in sight. We will have a normal release.' Then Disney put the biggest franchise of all time against us. I’m no fool. Those movies are a mammoth."

"So I was deeply disappointed," continued the director. "But we had committed to this date, to IMAX. It was impossible to move. So I accepted my fate, praying to the gods of cinema. Dune is not a mammoth like the Avengers, but it’s a sexy little animal that has a lot of firepower, and I hope we will survive. Both films have notably broken presales records . Dune: Part Three has reportedly bested Warner Bros. all-time presales record, selling more than $30 million worth of tickets for IMAX screens alone (the studio hasn't released its own all-theater presales numbers). But Doomsday has recently surpassed $100 million and has received the highest initial opening-weekend forecast in NRG tracking history ($270 million). So there's no world in which both films aren't big hits, but also no world in which Doomsday doesn't clock Dune on opening weekend.

Villeneuve also defended making some significant changes to Dune saga author Frank Herbert's source material for the third film, particularly in the storyline of Chani (Zendaya). "When you adapt, you kill," he said. "It is not the book. It is my movie inspired by the book, with tremendous respect … I had the idea to make Chani more of a critic regarding the idea of religious colonization … In the third movie, Chani is still a critic of the choices Paul has made. articles.content:
When Saturn Risin9 auditioned for Jordan Firstman’s “ Club Kid ,” her face was still swollen from facial feminization surgery. The musician, DJ and nightlife fixture, who had undergone the procedure a month earlier in April 2025, hadn't even attempted to put on a wig since her surgery. Unable to bring herself to let anyone into her apartment, she played all three characters in her self-tape.

“I think they were just like, ‘Who is this crazy lady?’” Risin9 recalls with a laugh. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Samantha Morton to Receive BFI Fellowship

Firstman, a longtime friend from the nightlife circuit, had told Risin9 at a party two years earlier that he was writing a role for her. But the audition request came just weeks after her gender-affirming surgery. For Risin9, the timing felt like an affirmation — "I thought it was so aligned, at the moment that I was so authentic with myself, that the world opened up to me," she says.

Now, Risin9 is one of the breakout stars of Firstman's A24 comedy-drama, which follows a New York City party promoter whose life is upended by the arrival of a son he never knew he had. As Saffron, a DJ with a protective streak and diva sensibilities, Risin9 brings to the film two decades of experience navigating underground nightlife.

The Bay Area native grew up performing in theater productions and wrote her first play at 11, but turned her attention to music in her 20s after finding that the acting roles available to her didn't align with her identity. She built a career as an independent recording artist, DJ and performer, touring internationally before relocating to Los Angeles in 2017. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Perhaps most gratifying to Risin9 has been the film's reception among audiences far removed from the world it depicts. After a screening at Telluride Film Festival, she was approached by a father who was crying in the arms of his daughter. "I was like, 'Are you okay?,'" she recalls. "And he was like, 'Your movie was just so beautiful.'"

Even Risin9's mother, who has historically been less comfortable watching queer intimacy on screen, ("She likes to pretend that she can't watch people make out and I'm like, 'I think you just don't want to see gay stuff') came away a fan.

The film's success also comes at a particularly exciting moment for queer cinema. In addition to "Club Kid," stories centered on gay men — such as "Elsinore," "La Bola Negra" and "Artificial" — dominate awards season buzz this year. "These films exist in a post-'Heated Rivalry' moment during which audiences seem newly open to queer stories," Variety's Dan D'Addario wrote last month, posing the question: is this the gayest Oscar season ever? "These films launch into surprising directions, showing many different sides of the gay experience."

Risin9 similarly describes this era as the "de-'Will & Grace’-ification of queer art,” in which LGBTQ stories are increasingly afforded the complexity, specificity and messiness that Hollywood has long granted their heterosexual counterparts. "Straight people want to see more things that they don't know about," she says. "We all want to learn. We don't want to stagnate."

Below, Risin9 talks about her audition process, her evolving relationship with nightlife and teaching her young co-star Reggie Absolom to DJ:

Léa Seydoux told me that she loved me in “Club Kid.” She just comes up to me and goes “I love you in the movie,” and I was like, “You saw ‘Club Kid’?” She was like, “I loved it,” and we actually walked the red carpet for “Gentle Monster” in Cannes. So it was kind of a kismet moment.

She had that knowingness that she was giving me something. You know what I mean? Like, “I have to tell you this, and you're gonna live for it.” It was so cute.

I didn't want to be too aware of what was happening because something that I love about acting is letting go and finding that space where you know the rhythm of it and you know what your cues are, but you're also allowing for the character to be thinking and to be human instead of just waiting to perform. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The first scene that we shot was the one where we go to Peter’s [Firstman's] house and find out that he has Arlo, and we're all busting in the house. I was supposed to say a few words about convincing him to do this party — and I was saying it so big, and Jordan just goes, "Just say it.” And I was like, “Oh, okay.”

That was what Jordan's direction always was. It was a lot of trust, but also the encouragement to be comfortable in it and not to be so showy.

Jordan and I were very friendly party friends. We've always had a really good rapport, and we hung out once in Atlanta. I brought my little cousin with me and I'm very protective of my family. I'm the disciplinarian. So I think he got to see that outside of the "most fun girl at the party," I’m also this maternal, super supportive figure. And I think his wheels started to turn.

I saw him about two years later at a party, and he was like, “Hey, I wrote this movie and I wrote a role for you. Would you be in my movie?” It's like 5 a.m. So I'm like, “Yeah, girl, whatever.” You know how many people stop me at the end of the night and say, “Oh my God, it would be so cool if we did this?”

I showed up in a fully laced bodysuit, thinking that they wanted to see a club diva. So I'm in this lace bodysuit at 10 a.m. in Hollywood. And I thought they wanted one of those nasty girls. I was reading it kind of cunty.

And then at the end, Carmen Cuba, our casting director, was like, “Can you do it more empathetic?” And I was like, “Okay, that's me! Let's talk. Let's go.”

There's a line in the movie where it's like, “When's the last time you saw a kid?” And I was like, really, actually, when was the last time I saw a kid? Because I also didn't know if he knew trans people. I was in my head. The last time I saw a kid, the kid was bullying me. So I was like, “Whoa!” Kids can be scary. And he could be a bro who just randomly got cast in this queer movie.

So I was just so surprised at how well-adjusted and kind and really cool he is. We were going over these vinyl and I'm like, “Do you like this one?” He's like, “No, I like heavy metal.” And I was like, “Oh!” blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I really did teach him how to DJ because Twitter is a scary place, and I'd hate for someone to zoom in on the movie and be like, "Why are you turning those knobs?" Now we’ve done DJ sets together and he actually knows what he's doing.

I think this might be the first year where I'm not seeing the shortcomings. I'm seeing incredibly different stories. I love that "Club Kid” is like the de-"Will & Grace”-ification of queer art because that was that safety that they were selling in the '90s and it kind of kept going for so long. Like, “Oh, we're just kind of quirky, normal people who like to shop,” or something. And it's just so much realer than that.

And even “La Bola Negra” being this Odyssey-level film. It's incredible that there are so many different avenues of our lives and our fantasies being shown in the way that everything else is shown in the world because it's normal. Life is normal for the people that are living it, and many people live many different lives.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One of the MCU 's biggest criticisms is that so many of its movies share a similar narrative structure, sense of humor, and tonal balance. Films like Iron Man and The Avengers have ensured that the influence of filmmakers like Jon Favreau and Joss Whedon, respectively, is felt long after they’ve vacated the director’s chair. After all, in many respects, the MCU’s true auteur is Kevin Feige himself, who has overseen the MCU and whose time working on Marvel movies dates back to the original X-Men in 2000. But every once in a while, a filmmaker has brought such a clear vision to a project that it unmistakably bears the trademarks of their other films.

James Gunn is absolutely one of the biggest examples of this. Before Guardians of the Galaxy , Gunn had only directed a pair of very dark, very R-rated genre films in 2006’s Slither and 2010’s Super . And it is Gunn’s storytelling voice and more unconventional sensibilities that made his work with Marvel stand out, to the point that so many people (including his Guardians cast) stood by him after his short-lived firing from Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 . Even now, years after Gunn left Marvel, the MCU carries much of his creative stamp. Avengers: Doomsday may be the ultimate example of Gunn’s impact on the MCU.

Let’s consider the little that we know for sure about Avengers: Doomsday . The film — directed by Joe and Anthony Russo — serves as the first Avengers film since Avengers: Endgame , it sees not just one but multiple teams from throughout the multiverse unite against a common threat. The Avengers led by Sam Wilson, the New Avengers led by Yelena Belova, the Wakandans, the Fox X-Men, and the newly minted MCU Fantastic Four will all inevitably cross paths, face off against each other, and ultimately unite to prevent Doctor Doom from realizing his mysterious plan. In part, this sounds like a bit of Avengers: Infinity War . But boiled down to its essence, the story sees a group of misfits forced to overcome their petty differences and come together by truly becoming a team.

That sounds an awful lot like the found family theme Gunn employed to spectacular effect in Guardians of the Galaxy , its sequels, and 2021’s The Suicide Squad . The biggest difference is that, instead of a group of five individuals with their own motivations and paths, Avengers: Doomsday expands that out into five teams of heroes. Granted, 2012’s The Avengers and 2025’s Thunderbolts* tread some similar ground in their team-building narratives. But Gunn has made found family one of his trademarks, and arguably few people in current superhero cinema do it better than him.

It says a lot about Gunn’s contributions to the MCU that so much of Marvel Studios' recent output resembles his work, which makes sense since it looked unlikely he would return to Marvel anytime soon. Of course, Gunn’s recent departure from DC Studios raises the possibility that he might return to working within the MCU. After all, he initially ended up working with DC on The Suicide Squad after Disney fired him from Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3 . So it stands to reason that he might hop back over to the other side of the street once his time at DC concludes. Right now, it’s unclear if 2027’s Man of Tomorrow will be the final DC project he works on before he leave.

If that’s the case, Marvel might be able to get Gunn involved in any number of upcoming projects. Both he and Marvel seem to be in no rush to make another Guardians of the Galaxy film, despite star Chris Pratt's interest . Reportedly, the next few years of the MCU will center on the Mutant Saga, and if there’s any Marvel property that feels ripe for Gunn to apply his particular brand of found family superheroes to, it’s the X-Men. It’s challenging to predict which project best to mark Gunn’s potential MCU return, since so little is known about what’s next. But he should absolutely be in the mix to play in the X-Men sandbox.

Should James Gunn return to the MCU? If so, which project should he take on? Let us know your thoughts in the comments!

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters on December 18, 2026.

articles.summary: Mitte's family continue to mourn the actor.
articles.content:
The holidays are a great time to be around family and celebrate their company, but they are always more difficult when you’ve just lost a loved one. Breaking Bad cast member RJ Mitte died on October 12, 2026, at the age of 34 by suicide. The loss is still fresh for his mother and sister, and they took some time to publicly pay tribute to him on Thanksgiving.

Mitte’s mom shared a photo of herself with RJ Mitte and his sister Lacianne Carriere. She wrote that she’s “missing” him on Thanksgiving, but she “made all [his] favorites”. RJ’s sister also took to her Instagram account to share a throwback photo with the late actor. Here it is:

RJ’s younger sister expressed that she’s “thankful for the time” she had with her brother, and is really feeling his absence on the first holiday she and her family are spending without him. About a month ago, Carriere took to the platform to share a long tribute to RJ, calling him her “everything” and “other half”. It’s a particularly huge loss for his closest relatives.

Mitte’s body was found by his mother on the morning of October 12 in his home in Brownville, Texas. His official cause of death was ruled a suicide the same day. His mother said she had offered and suggested her son go to therapy in the three months before his passing, but he said he was “OK” and “handling it” (via Today ).

As people traveled back home for Thanksgiving, a lot of moviegoers made a stop at Panem to return to the world of "The Hunger Games." The new prequel, "Sunrise on the Reaping," ruled the Thanksgiving box office with $11.6 million on Thursday.

Lionsgate's latest entry in the YA action franchise will dominate the box office for the second week in a row. articles.summary: After the loss of Patrick Stewart this October, Kevin Feige has shared an anecdote about the late star on the set of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness—and it involves some Star Trek spoilers. Marvel fans, Star Trek fans, and innumerable fans of Patrick Stewart's work in general were devastated last month when it […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google After the loss of Patrick Stewart this October, Kevin Feige has shared an anecdote about the late star on the set of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness —and it involves some Star Trek spoilers. Marvel fans, Star Trek fans, and innumerable fans of Patrick Stewart's work in general were devastated last month when it was confirmed that Stewart had passed. This also means that his role as Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday will be the storied actor's final on-screen appearance , making it all the more significant and notable. That wasn't Stewart's first appearance in the MCU, though. That occurred several years ago, in Multiverse of Madness .

As audiences anxiously await the arrival of Doomsday in just a few weeks, which will finally offer fans that look at Stewart's last performance, Feige has provided a hilarious anecdote from on the set of Multiverse of Madness in an interview with Entertainment Weekly . Apparently, while filming that movie, Feige, who is a self-proclaimed Trekkie, didn't even have to poke Stewart a bit for some answers regarding the TV series Star Trek: Picard . While one might suspect that Stewart would keep any such details tightly under wraps, Feige found that was far from the case. Check out Feige's exact comments below.

Speaking to Entertainment Weekly about his time on set with Stewart, Feige shared that he didn't even have to push for Picard spoilers, saying, "He volunteered a few, and then I told him to stop. I just wanted to watch and enjoy the show." It's funny to imagine this dynamic, in which Stewart is readily offering up spoilers for the show, so much so that Feige has to stop him because he's genuinely enjoying the series, but it also suggests a friendliness between Stewart and Feige on set that is nice to imagine, especially considering that they reunited for Doomsday .

It will also be interesting to see how Stewart's role in Doomsday is different from that of Multiverse of Madness —especially because many fans are hoping to see quite a bit more power from Charles Xavier in Doomsday , following his death in Multiverse of Madness , in which the Scarlet Witch snapped his neck. Granted, that was meant to showcase just how powerful Wanda was at that point, and it did so, but X-Men fans were still largely disappointed with this fate and wanted to see more from Professor X. Presumably, they finally will with Doomsday , and hopefully, that will be a proper send off for the star who absolutely deserves some major moments of heroism in the upcoming movie. Either way, though, it will be very sad to see the movie conclude and know that this iconic actor is no longer with us.
